seo.title: Le Choiseul: Amboise Riverside Hotel Review 2026
seo.description: 18th-century Amboise mansion on the Loire below the royal château. Score 80/100, from €320/night. Best room, 7-night itinerary.

content.verdict: Le Choiseul is the most central Loire honeymoon hotel — an 18th-century mansion that was once the Duke of Choiseul's town residence, now a 36-room four-star directly below the royal château of Amboise with a garden running down to the Loire river. The defining advantage is location: walk five minutes uphill to the château gate, ten minutes to the Clos Lucé where Leonardo lived his last years, and zero minutes to the riverside path that the local cyclists use for the Loire à Vélo. The Pavillon main building holds the historic rooms with the river views; a converted hunting cottage and a small modern annex round out the 36 rooms. The restaurant is a classic French traditional kitchen (not Michelin but consistently good), the pool sits in the walled garden with the château looming above, and the breakfast on the river terrace is the small moment that justifies the booking. What you get at Choiseul versus the surrounding country properties (Pray, Artigny, Hauts de Loire) is town walkability — for couples who want to walk to the château and the village restaurants in the evening rather than driving everywhere, Choiseul is the answer. The trade-off is that the property is in the town centre with some street noise, and the spa is minimal. Pair with rental car for château touring (Chenonceau 20 min, Chambord 50 min) and you have a romantic, walkable, value-tier Loire honeymoon base.
content.best_room: The Privilège category rooms in the main mansion with full Loire-river views and small balconies — the canonical romantic rooms. The Suite Choiseul on the top floor is the celebrity-press suite with a wraparound terrace over the river. Avoid the modern annex rooms (Catégorie Confort) — they look at the back garden and miss the entire Choiseul magic.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Arrival from Paris
itinerary_7_nights.description: TGV from Paris Montparnasse to Tours St-Pierre-des-Corps (1h), 25-minute drive east to Amboise. Park at the hotel, walk five minutes up the cobbles to the royal château of Amboise for the late-afternoon visit. Dinner at the Choiseul restaurant on the river terrace.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Clos Lucé
itinerary_7_nights.description: 10-minute walk to the Clos Lucé — Leonardo da Vinci's last home (1516-1519), the period rooms, the workshop, and the garden full of full-scale working models of Leonardo's inventions. Lunch at L'Écluse on the river. Late afternoon at the Choiseul pool.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Chenonceau
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive 25 minutes east to Chenonceau for the 8:30am opening — the river gallery, the gardens, the kitchens. Lunch at L'Orangerie. Afternoon walking the Loire river path back at Amboise.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Chambord
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive 50 minutes north-east to Chambord — the 426-room Renaissance hunting lodge, Leonardo's double-helix staircase, the rooftop terraces. Lunch at the village. Return via Chaumont-sur-Loire's clifftop château.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Vouvray Wine Day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive 25 minutes south to Vouvray for the day — tastings at Domaine Huet, Champalou, and Domaine du Clos Naudin. Lunch at Restaurant Le Cèdre. Evening at the Choiseul terrace with a bottle from the cellar.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Loire à Vélo Cycle
itinerary_7_nights.description: Rent electric bikes from Détours de Loire next door for the Amboise-to-Chaumont stretch (25km flat along the dedicated cycle path). Lunch at a village along the way. Late afternoon by the pool.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Slow Morning and Departure
itinerary_7_nights.description: Final breakfast on the river terrace, a last walk up to the royal château, and the drive back to Tours station.

caveats: Choiseul is in the centre of Amboise — there is some town street noise on the side rooms, especially on summer weekend nights. Specify river-side rooms (Privilège category) at booking.
The spa is small — a single treatment room and a sauna. For a real spa day, drive to Hauts de Loire (30 min) or Artigny (40 min).
The pool is in the walled garden, small (12 metres), and gets sun-loungers crowded by 11am in peak season.

faqs.question: Good for honeymooners?
faqs.answer: Choiseul is the walkable-town Loire honeymoon — five minutes to the royal château, ten to the Clos Lucé, river-terrace breakfast. Best for couples who want town walkability and the value tier rather than full Relais & Châteaux country isolation.

faqs.question: Best time to visit?
faqs.answer: May through September. May for the gardens and the river light, September for the harvest and the quieter châteaux. October works for the autumn colour. November-March is dead for the region.

faqs.question: Book in advance?
faqs.answer: 2-4 months ahead for the river-view Privilège rooms. Suite Choiseul books 4-6 months ahead. Direct booking via the hotel — small family-style management is helpful with honeymoon arrangements.

faqs.question: Adults-only?
faqs.answer: No — Choiseul accepts families but the size and the focus mean the guest mix is heavily couples and culture-focused travellers.

faqs.question: Best room type?
faqs.answer: Privilège category in the main mansion with full river views. Suite Choiseul on the top floor for the wraparound terrace. Skip the Confort modern annex rooms.

faqs.question: How to get there?
faqs.answer: TGV from Paris Montparnasse to Tours St-Pierre-des-Corps (1h), 25-minute drive east to Amboise. Amboise also has its own SNCF station with regional trains from Tours (15 min). Rent a car at Tours station for château touring.
